page_title: TetherShot — iPhone screenshots, delivered to your Mac

summary.name: TetherShot
summary.one_liner: A native macOS app that captures full-resolution iPhone screenshots over USB or local Wi-Fi and saves them to a folder and the clipboard, without a cloud relay.
use_cases: Capture iPhone screenshots at full resolution for docs or bug reports
Grab phone screens for app store or marketing mockups
Take cable-free iPhone screenshots over local Wi-Fi
Quickly copy a phone screen into chat or an editor
Screenshot Android phones connected via adb from a Mac
summary.what_it_does: TetherShot is a native macOS utility that pulls the iPhone's screen frame over a USB cable using AVFoundation, or over local Wi-Fi using Apple's developer-services tunnel via pymobiledevice3. Each capture is saved to a chosen folder and copied to the clipboard, and a global hotkey (⌘⇧7) triggers it. It can run with an optional menu-bar controller, and closing the window keeps capture running. The page also says authorized Android phones can be captured via adb screencap over USB or wireless debugging. The page states that no analytics, account or server is involved.
notable: Wi-Fi capture works even when the iPhone is locked, after one-time USB pairing and Developer Mode
Installs via Homebrew cask, signed universal DMG, or npm CLI
Local-only: screenshots go straight to folder and clipboard with no cloud relay
Merges USB and Wi-Fi appearances of the same phone into one device entry
caveats: Wi-Fi capture requires a one-time USB pairing, Developer Mode, and the pymobiledevice3 tunnel service (admin password needed for setup)
Requires macOS 14+ and Xcode Command Line Tools
USB capture relies on the Camera privacy permission because macOS exposes the mirrored screen through the camera pipeline
